September inflation is forecast at 5.9% after 6.2% in August and 6.5% in July, following an extended period of monetary tightening and rising bank reserve ratio requirements. It may be that the press is jumping the gun somewhat, but either way, the Chinese population remains a strong buyer of gold. Pre-existing fears over inflation and/ or a property bubble have been stimulating gold buying for much of this year and this is unlikely to change. • Neutral: To this end the impact of Operation Twist may be significant as it means that the Fed will be buying longer-term maturities, which should help to keep mortgage rates

down and should also have a ripple effect into other securities as price discovery mechanisms lead investors to diversify away from the long end and into other asset classes. The fact that Operation Twist should be net neutral in terms of money supply could be seen as negative for gold (because it reduces the fears of yet more inflationary expectations), but if anything, it should be supportive as it underpins, if not extends, the likely period of negative real interest rates. • Neutral / mildly positive: The fact that the FOMC came up with a policy that does not involve the injection of additional liquidity originally received the thumbs-down from the investment fraternity, but is now gaining favour. Arguably, this works against gold, but, equally, there are no signs of liquidity being drained from the system. • Pro for the short term at least: uncertainty over the acceptability of President Obama’s deficit-cutting proposals will be supportive until the vote (which is due on 23rd November, the day before Thanksgiving Day. History implies that this vote will “go to the wire” with plenty of brinkmanship beforehand; the proposal to raise taxes by $1.5 trillion is already meeting opposition from the Republican Party. • Pro: Inflationary forces have also been rising in Asia. Food inflation is particularly strong and, while Chinese headline overall inflation in August was 6.2% year-on-year against 6.5% in July, domestic food prices in August were up by 13.4% year-on-year. The government’s monetary policies, with continued tightening of bank reserve ratio requirementx and rising interest rates, may be taking some heat out of the economy, but local investors are remaining strong gold buyers as they are concerned about longer-term inflation, or a property bubble, or both. Taking these and other arguments into account, and looking at the trading patterns of late September, we believe that our medium-term expectations for a recovery in gold in the fourth quarter of this year remains valid; and that the fundamentals (including investor attitudes) point towards elevated prices throughout 2012.
